title: Verifier‑Grounded Intent→Config Evaluation with Shared‑Initial Semantics: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We present a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini; model_config SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one canonical LLM candidate generated per task and reused for both scoring conditions), all confirmatory episodes completed with baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded (gpt‑5‑mini) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish exhaustive execution and scoring artifacts with per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints so others can deterministically replay and audit every step (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the submitted bundle), (ii) use those artifacts to diagnose why the preregistered paired contrast is degenerate (identical canonical candidates + template‑tight tasks + deterministic validator), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversification, expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the independent generative‑reliability question practitioners require.

sections.introduction:
Translating high‑level operator intent into device configurations is a routine but safety‑sensitive NetOps activity: incorrect sequences or transient states can break reachability, violate ACLs, or create unsafe failover windows. Deterministic offline validators that analyze static configurations for reachability, ACL equivalence, and routing invariants (Batfish style) provide an auditable oracle for pre‑deployment correctness [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Large language models (LLMs) enable fast natural‑language→config generation, but their stochastic outputs raise operational reliability questions: what is the probability that an independently drawn LLM candidate satisfies an operational verifier? This study preregistered a narrower, precisely specified estimand—verifier consistency under identical inputs—and executed a fully artifact‑anchored pipeline to (1) report exact confirmatory counts and inferential statistics grounded in archived traces and (2) diagnose, from those same artifacts, why the paired contrast is uninformative for independent generative reliability.

Research question, estimand, and contributions. The preregistered primary research question asked: Does a single‑pass LLM generator (gpt‑5‑mini) have a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline across N = 120 tasks? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed under generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (i.e., a single canonical LLM output per task reused for both conditions). Our contributions are: (A) a reproducible, byte‑for‑byte artifact bundle (model/provider call traces, per‑episode validator JSON traces, seeds, and full SHA‑256 manifest) that supports exact reruns; (B) the confirmatory outcome and preregistered statistical inference (baseline = 120/120, guarded = 120/120, paired diff = 0.00; bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0); and (C) an artifact‑grounded analysis diagnosing why the shared_initial design yields a degenerate paired table and how to rerun the pipeline deterministically to answer independent reliability questions.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation. Offline semantic validators and configuration analysis tools (Batfish and successors) operate by computing forwarding/reachability and semantic checks from static device configs; they are a standard operational pattern for pre‑deployment validation and have been scaled to real networks [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Prior LLM→NetOps studies adopt variants of the generate–validate–repair pattern: generator proposes candidates, verifier applies deterministic checks, and an orchestrator / repair loop attempts fixes. Methodological axes that vary across prior work and materially affect inference are (i) sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs independent per‑condition sampling), (ii) repair budget (single pass vs bounded iterative repair), and (iii) validator scope (syntactic parsing vs reachability+ACL+routing checks). Studies that use independent sampling and multi‑seed replication directly estimate generative reliability; studies that reuse canonical candidates test validator and scoring reproducibility. Our artifact corpus and diagnosis align with and extend these methodological observations (see also 2024–2026 intent→config studies [10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407; 10.1002/nem.70029]).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. The full preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) was frozen before observing outputs (SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). Key preregistered elements: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), model = declared_model_version gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, confirmatory generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, initial per‑pair canonical seed_0, analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 with 10,000 bootstrap resamples (seed = 1729). The manifest and every file hash are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json) to permit deterministic reruns.

Task synthesis and template semantics. Tasks were programmatically synthesized by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 into a template bank encoding: initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence (the minimal safe sequence), workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty annotations. Representative task manifests and canonical candidate files are published in the bundle (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt). This template tightness was intentional to encode operationally meaningful transient constraints (make‑before‑break, atomic MTU changes) that the deterministic validator checks.

Generation, orchestration, and model calls. The orchestration used adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and produced one shared_initial_candidate per task which was recorded at execution/responses/task-000###-shared-initial.txt (representative SHA‑256s: task‑000001 SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080; task‑000002 SHA‑256 ae967f70dfb6ccb8b5dbcb1491775f30b8b06497cd3020139285aacbb13f491e). The preregistered counting rule yields model_calls_used = 120 because the shared canonical generation was produced once per pair and reused for both scoring episodes. The provider call traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json and the call cache under execution/call_cache/* so exact provider interactions and timings can be inspected deterministically.

Deterministic validator and scoring. Each candidate was scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) under scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation: a binary pass requires that (a) the required_sequence is present in an order satisfying workflow_policies, (b) transient constraints (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups) hold during the change, and (c) final_state invariants (reachability/ACL) are satisfied. Each scoring episode produced a structured JSON trace archived at execution/scoring/task-000###-*.json (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57fff893fe02bd395c435a422f5431376e439875577a8431063), which records parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration and validation_after.valid.

Confirmatory analysis protocol. The primary estimator is the mean over i=1..120 of (guarded_i − baseline_i), with inference via a 10,000‑resample percentile bootstrap (seed = 1729) and an exact McNemar two‑sided test on the paired 2×2 table. Missingness and infrastructure failures were to be handled per preregistered rules; none occurred (completed_episode_count = 240, failed_episode_count = 0). All analysis code and derived CSVs are archived (analysis/*).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw confirmatory counts. Planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial canonical generation per pair counted once); maximum_model_calls = 240. The full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256s are in execution/execution_manifest.json (manifest includes execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820 and the initial master prompt provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Confirmatory outcomes (preregistered). Baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. The paired contingency table is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaafb3562e0710e0cf10b7a47a55ea00fcbcf02eee324f79afafe7). Primary estimand = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f37c4b6ff5aa20ab9745b872be94e75861cabc8a1b636b246ab1610b7; analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c644f8cf7579ff0b2daec77475310d4de96da6a4f1a9266a6ebd72aad) are archived and reproduce these numbers.

Representative validator trace evidence. Per‑episode validator JSON traces show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration and validation_after.valid = true for canonical candidates. Example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57fff893fe02bd395c435a422f5431376e439875577a8431063) records parsed_command_count = 4 and validation_after.valid = true for the canonical candidate stored at execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...). Similar archived traces exist for all 120 pairs and permit deterministic inspection of exactly why a candidate passed.

Artifact‑visible causal chain to degeneracy. The confirmatory degeneracy (all pairs n_11) is explained deterministically by two preregistered, archived design choices visible in the bundle: (1) generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one canonical LLM output archived per task at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt and reused identically for baseline and guarded scoring), and (2) template‑tight task synthesis that encodes explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies the canonical candidates were designed to satisfy. Because the validator is deterministic, identical inputs must yield identical pass/fail outputs; the execution and scoring artifacts establish this causal chain byte‑for‑byte.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and correct scope. The confirmatory statistics are correct for the preregistered estimand—verifier response to identical canonical inputs—but they do not estimate the operationally central quantity of independent generative reliability (the probability that independently drawn LLM candidates satisfy validator constraints). The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally controlled candidate content to test scoring reproducibility; that control both motivated the preregistration and is the reason the paired contingency collapsed. Readers and practitioners must therefore not infer independent sampling reliability from the confirmatory counts without additional runs using independent_per_condition sampling.

Runnable, artifact‑grounded next steps. The full archive permits deterministically reproducible reruns that answer independent reliability questions while preserving preregistration provenance: (A) independent_per_condition confirmatory rerun — generate two independent seeds per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and recompute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design — draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities via bootstrap; (C) validator diversification — run an additional, independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates to reduce validator–task coupling. All required artifacts for these reruns are published: execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/call_cache/*.json. Because every file and seed is archived with SHA‑256, the reruns are deterministic and fully auditable.

Threats to validity and methodological lessons. Internal validity: the shared_initial design removes generation variance and therefore cannot test independent generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑tight tasks plus a single deterministic validator increase the chance of canonical candidate success and reduce generality to open, paraphrased intents. External validity: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization to other model families and real operator language. Conclusion validity: a degenerate 2×2 table yields trivial but correct inferential outputs; interpreting them beyond the preregistered estimand is incorrect. The practical methodological lesson is that (i) verifier grounding is necessary for auditable correctness checks, and (ii) experimental generation semantics must match the deployment question—shared canonical candidates test validator reproducibility; independent per‑condition sampling measures model reliability under deployment stochasticity. Publishing exhaustive artifacts (responses, scoring traces, provider calls, and per‑file SHA‑256s) materially reduces ambiguity about what a confirmatory test actually measured and permits immediate, deterministic rectifications.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released an exhaustive artifact bundle permitting byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json contains the full file list and SHA‑256 manifest). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and gpt‑5‑mini canonical candidates passed all N = 120 verifier checks (120/120 each). Archived evidence demonstrates identical canonical candidates per pair plus template‑tight tasks and a deterministic validator caused the degenerate paired contingency; therefore the confirmatory result is not informative about independent LLM generative reliability. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications—independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, and validator diversification—that convert the run into an informative operational comparison without sacrificing reproducibility. All execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts (including initial master prompt provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba and preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) are included in the submission bundle to enable exact audit and deterministic follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
